name: Proton Mail Bridge
description: Sign in to Proton Mail Bridge and keep your mail connected in the background
author: spotty
help:
Trigger: proton (optional Store install)

Type "proton login" or "proton gui" to open the optional Spotty Proton Mail Bridge login window if installed. Build and install the native companion with Cargo from this repository's proton-bridge-gui folder. The companion supports username, masked account password, two-factor code, separate mailbox password, and security-key PIN. Fields appear when Bridge asks for them. Never enter passwords in Spotty's search bar.

In the companion, use Start Bridge if it is not running, then sign in. Bridge manages saved accounts in its own keyring. The startup checkbox controls Bridge's Open on startup setting. Close and keep Bridge running leaves the mail bridge connected.

Only one frontend can own Bridge login. If the official Bridge GUI is already running, use that window or choose Quit Bridge there before starting the companion. Human verification and setup problems are handed to the official GUI. Opening the official GUI from the companion may briefly restart a headless Bridge.

Type "proton open" to use the official Bridge window directly. Without the companion, login/gui opens the official GUI too. Type "proton start" to launch the official Bridge app without showing its window, or "proton install" to open Proton's installation guide. Sign in once before starting in the background.

Requires native protonmail-bridge on PATH, a working Linux keyring, and a paid Proton plan that includes Mail. Configure your email client using the local IMAP/SMTP details and Bridge-generated password in the official GUI. This trigger does not install packages automatically. Removing it does not sign out or quit Bridge.

Companion: https://github.com/Aras1907/spotty-triggers/tree/main/proton-bridge-gui
Setup: https://proton.me/support/protonmail-bridge-install

action.command:
case {query} in
  login|gui)
    if command -v spotty-proton-bridge-gui >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      if ! command -v nohup >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s\n' 'nohup is required to launch the login window independently.' >&2; exit 1; fi
      nohup spotty-proton-bridge-gui </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
      printf '%s\n' 'Opening the Proton Mail Bridge login window.'
      exit 0
    elif [ -x "${HOME}/.cargo/bin/spotty-proton-bridge-gui" ]; then
      if ! command -v nohup >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s\n' 'nohup is required to launch the login window independently.' >&2; exit 1; fi
      nohup "${HOME}/.cargo/bin/spotty-proton-bridge-gui" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
      printf '%s\n' 'Opening the Proton Mail Bridge login window.'
      exit 0
    fi
    printf '%s\n' 'Optional Spotty login window is not installed. Opening the official Bridge GUI.'
    set -- ;;
  open) set -- ;;
  start) set -- --no-window ;;
  install) exec xdg-open https://proton.me/support/protonmail-bridge-install ;;
  help) printf '%s\n' 'proton login / proton gui: open the optional Cargo login window, or the official Bridge GUI.' 'proton open: open the official Bridge GUI.' 'proton start: launch Bridge in the background after signing in.' 'proton install: open the official installation guide.' 'In Bridge Settings, enable Open on startup to reconnect at desktop login.' 'Close the window to keep mail connected; Quit Bridge stops it.' 'Use the Bridge-generated password and local IMAP/SMTP settings in your mail client.' 'Requires native protonmail-bridge on PATH, a Linux keyring, and a paid Proton Mail plan.' 'Setup: https://proton.me/support/protonmail-bridge-install'; exit 0 ;;
  *) printf '%s\n' 'Use proton login, proton gui, proton open, proton start, proton install, or proton help. Enter credentials only in the login window.' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
if ! command -v protonmail-bridge >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s\n' 'Proton Mail Bridge is not installed or not on PATH. Opening the official installation guide.'
  exec xdg-open https://proton.me/support/protonmail-bridge-install
fi
if ! command -v nohup >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s\n' 'nohup is required to keep Bridge running after the launcher closes.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
nohup protonmail-bridge "$@" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
printf '%s\n' 'Launch requested. Bridge manages your login and background mail connection. For startup errors, open Bridge directly and check its logs.'
